who when he had not tound her, 21. he asked the men of that place:
Where is the woman that ſate in the croſſe way? Al tnak ing anſwer :
There was no harlot in this place, 22. he returned to Iudas, and ſaid
to him : I haue not tound her : vea the men alſo of that place ſaid vuto
me that there neuer ſate harlot there. 22. Iudas ſaid: Let her take it
to her, ſurely ſhe can not charge vs with a lye, I ſent the kid which I
promiſed: and thou dideſt not find her. 24. And behold after three
months they told Iudas, ſaying: Thamar thy daughter in law hath
plaved the harlot, and her bellie ſermeth to ſwel. And Iudas ſaid:
Bring her torth (c) that ſhe may be burnt. 25. Who when ſhe was led
to execution, ſhe ſent to her father in law , ſaying : By that man, whoſe
theſe things are, haue I conceaued : looke whoſe the ring is, and the
bracelet, and the ſtaffe. 26. Who acknowledging the guitts, ſaid : She
is iuſter then I: becauſe I did not giue her to Sela my ſonne. But he
knew ber no more. 27. And when the was readie to be brought to bed,
there appeared twinnes in her bellie : and in the verie deliuerie of the
infants one put torth the hand, wherin the midwite tyed a skarlet
ſtring, ſaying : 28. This ſhal come torth the former. 29. But he drawing
backe his hand, the other came forth: and the woman ſaid : Why is
the pat tition diuided for thee: and tor this cauſe called his nate Pha-
res.  Atterward his brother came torth, in Whoſe hand was the
skarlet ſtring: whom ſhe called Lara.

8. Raiſe ſeed to thy brother. ) By this it appeareth, that ia the law of nature,
when a maried man died without iffue, his brother might lawfully marie the
widow: whoſe firſt ſonne thould be counted and cailed the ſonne and hevre of
his vncle dead before. The ſame was eſtablished hy the law of Movſes ( Deut.5)
Which being now abrogated, it remaineth in the Churches power to conſtitute a
law in this behalf, and conſequently to diſpence in the ſame, ſo farre as is agrea-
ble with the law of nature. Wher of ſee more Leuit. 18.
